To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed the first universal BIOS/UEFI rootkit framework that runs on all x86-64 platforms and is capable of interacting with the operating system kernel.

“LONGKIT is a novel framework for malicious code in the BIOS/UEFI that is universal, fully written in position independent assembly, supports the 64bit Intel architecture and provides a full range of threats from malicious code in the System Management Mode.”
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: • The design of a framework for universal BIOS/UEFI rootkits in the SMM • The demonstration of the full potential of SMM malware by implementing a variety of malicious functionality, including the interception of keystrokes, the injection of code into user-mode applications, the modification of the system’s boot process, and the exfiltration of sensitive information • The implementation of a proof-of-concept rootkit based on the framework, which is capable of running on a variety of BIOS
demonstrating that the threat of malicious SMM code has not been sufficiently addressed and that there is a pressing need for novel research in the field of SMM security.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LONGKIT demonstrates that the BIOS/UEFI is a viable attack vector for a wide range of threats, from stealing credentials and sensitive data, to injecting malware into running applications and performing persistent attacks.
LONGKIT is the first universal framework for BIOS/ UEFI malware in the S.M.M. that is able to interact with the operating system in an advanced manner.
SMM rootkits are a serious threat to the security of computer systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LONGKIT is a universal framework for SMM malware in BIOS/UEFI that is fully written in assembly language.
we present an SMM rootkit framework which is universal in nature and can be used to evaluate SMM detection strategies.
we provide a novel framework for SMM malware that is universal and memory layout aware and thus can be used to evaluate SMM malware detection methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the threat of malicious code in BIOS/UEFI is real and should be taken seriously.

the SMM provides a powerful attack platform, but also that the threat of BIOS/UEFI rootkits can be significantly mitigated by applying existing techniques from the field of hypervisor malware detection.
the SMM provides the attacker with an unprecedented amount of capabilities and that the current state of SMM malware detection is far from sufficient.
